step1.wasteTooltip: Material loss allowance during transport and compaction (Standard 5-10%)

step2.distPowerTooltip: Main cable distance from power source to temporary main breaker
step2.distWaterTooltip: Main pipe distance from water source to temporary storage tank

step3.siteWidthTooltip: Refer to site width from Site Plan
step3.siteLengthTooltip: Refer to site length from Site Plan
step3.peakWorkersTooltip: Estimate peak workforce for camp and sanitation sizing

step4.bldgWidthTooltip: Measure distance from leftmost to rightmost column per structural plan
step4.bldgLengthTooltip: Measure distance from frontmost to backmost column per structural plan
step4.colCountTooltip: Count based on column grid intersections in foundation plan

step5.pileTypeTooltip: Refer to structural engineering general notes
step5.pileCountTooltip: Total count based on piling layout plan
step5.pileLengthTooltip: Refer to soil boring test report or engineer specification

step6.name: Label
step6.countTooltip: Identify count from foundation plan coordinates
step6.lengthLTooltip: Reference footprint length from structural footing details
step6.excDepthTooltip: Measured from ±0.00/existing ground to bottom of sand bed
step6.rebarWeightTooltip: Standard 80-140 kg/m³. For accuracy, replace with actual BBS data later.

step7.countTooltip: Identify pedestal count from foundation plan
step7.heightHTooltip: Distance from top of footing to ground/grade beam level

step8.totalLenTooltip: Calculate combined length of all ground beams from Ground Beam Plan
step8.widthBTooltip: Reference beam detail schedule. Typically 0.15-0.20 m
step8.heightHTooltip: Reference beam detail schedule. Typically 0.30-0.50 m
step8.leanThickTooltip: Standard 0.05-0.10 m below the ground beam

step9.areaTooltip: Measure total slab on grade area from the ground floor plan
step9.thicknessTooltip: Refer to slab details. Typically 0.10-0.15 m for residential areas
step9.sandThickTooltip: Refer to typical slab section. Usually 0.05-0.10 m for leveling
step9.plasticFactorTooltip: Plastic sheet per slab area including overlaps. Typically 1.10-1.15 m²
step9.perimeterTooltip: Used to calculate edge formwork length
step9.edgeFormworkLenTooltip: If left empty, computed automatically from slab perimeter
step9.slopePctTooltip: Required for drainage paths or garage ramps
step9.screedDaysTooltip: Duration of using a vibrating screed for finishing

step10.areaTooltip: Measure total precast slab area from floor plans
step10.toppingThickTooltip: Cast-in-place concrete over precast planks. Typically 0.05-0.07 m
step10.shearKeyTooltip: Indicate if grouted shear keys are required for diaphragm action
step10.spanTooltip: Clear span affecting panel count and temporary shoring
step10.panelWidthTooltip: Hollow-core: typically 1.20 m / Plank: typically 0.35 m
step10.panelThickTooltip: For precise volume calculation. Typically 0.12 m
step10.screedDaysTooltip: Duration of vibrating screed and finishing operations

step11.countTooltip: Sum quantity of this column type from Column Schedule
step11.heightTooltip: Clear distance from floor level to beam soffit
step11.rebarDensityTooltip: Lower floors 120-150 kg/m³ | Upper floors 150-200 kg/m³

step12.countTooltip: Count of this beam type from Beam Schedule
step12.slabAreaTooltip: Measure total slab area from structural floor plan
step12.slabThickTooltip: Standard 0.12–0.15 m. Roof deck should be ≥ 0.12 m
step12.rebarDensityTooltip: Combine factors for beams + slab: 130-180 kg/m³
step12.floorHeightTooltip: Required to calculate shoring quantity (Standard ~3 m)

step13.flightCountTooltip: 1 Flight = straight run of stairs between landings. Enter 0 if no stairs.
step13.stepsPerFlightTooltip: Number of treads in a single flight (excluding landings)
step13.stairRiseTooltip: Ref to stair detail. Typically 0.17-0.19 m (max 0.20 m by code)
step13.stairGoingTooltip: Distance from edge of nosing to face of riser. Typically 0.25-0.275 m
step13.stairWidthTooltip: Clear distance from edge to edge without handrails. Typically 1.00-1.20 m
step13.landingAreaTooltip: Combined WxL for all landings in this staircase
step13.waistThickTooltip: Thickness of the structural slab acting as the stair waist. Typically 0.15 m

step14.plateCountTooltip: Count all columns receiving steel structures from structural/roof plans
step14.boltCountTooltip: Number of bolts per base plate (typically 4/plate)
step14.boltDiameterTooltip: Example: 4-M16 J-Bolt means 4 bolts of M16 size
step14.boltTemplateTooltip: Template formwork to position bolts securely during pour

step15.roofAreaTooltip: Horizontal projection area (W×L) from the roof plan, including eaves
step15.roofShapeTooltip: Lean-to is the most economical; Hip requires the most steel due to valley rafters
step15.roofPitchTooltip: Refer to elevations. E.g., 5° (Metal Sheet) or 30° (Concrete Tile)
step15.heavyTileTooltip: Check if using concrete/ceramic tiles (>35 kg/m²) to account for heavier steel framing
step15.weldingRodTooltip: Percentage of total structural steel weight

step16.slopeAreaTooltip: Area along the roof pitch. Can be estimated as Plan Area ÷ Cos(PitchAngle)
step16.roofingTypeTooltip: Concrete Tile (CPAC), Ceramic, Metal Sheet, etc.
step16.ridgeTooltip: Highest horizontal line of the roof
step16.hipTooltip: Diagonal sloping ridge lines (for Hip roofs)
step16.eaveTooltip: Perimeter length of the overhanging roof edge
step16.insulationTooltip: Reflective foil installed over purlins before roofing
step16.birdBlockTooltip: Installed at eaves to prevent birds from nesting

step17.grossWallTooltip: Total Width × Height of all walls (floor to beam)
step17.openingsTooltip: Area of doors and windows to subtract from gross wall area
step17.wasteTooltip: Typically 10-15% for clay bricks and 5-10% for AAC blocks
step17.lintelTooltip: Concrete perimeters for doors/windows and wide walls to prevent cracking

step18.openingsTooltip: Area of doors+windows in this room

step19.widthTooltip: Measured from interior wall to interior wall
step19.dropTooltip: Recessed / drop ceiling uses roughly 50% more framing
step19.corniceTooltip: If left blank, auto-calculated from perimeter of all rooms

step20.patternTooltip: Diagonal pattern creates more breakage waste (approx. 15%)
step20.skirtingTooltip: If left blank, auto-calculated from perimeter of all rooms

step21.widthTooltip: Measured interior wall-to-wall from floor plan
step21.lengthTooltip: Measured interior wall-to-other-wall from floor plan
step21.wallTileTooltip: Typically tiled to ceiling 2.40m, some designs only tile up to 1.20m.
step21.waterproofTooltip: Standard: wet zone 1.80m, dry zone 0.30m. Enter an average value to use.
step21.wasteTooltip: Bathrooms typically need a 15% waste margin due to more corners and cuts.

step22.facadeTooltip: Measure from all elevations, subtracting doors and windows. Only include areas that require finishing materials (not the whole wall if partially finished).
step22.finishTooltip: If using paint only, this calculation is skipped and handled in Step 25.
step22.sealantTooltip: Perimeter around windows and cladding edges using PU Sealant.

step23.intAreaTooltip: Directly calculated from Interior Plastering area (Step 18)
step23.intPrimerTooltip: New concrete ≤ 6 months → Alkali Seal | Old concrete → Acrylic
step23.extPrimerTooltip: Cracked exterior wall → Elastomeric | New concrete → Alkali Seal
step23.coatsTooltip: Usually 1 coat, apply 2 coats if heavy alkali present on new concrete.
step23.sandTooltip: New concrete walls usually require sanding to remove residual cement splashes.
step23.fillCracksTooltip: Hairline cracks should be filled with acrylic sealant before priming.

step24.sealantTooltip: If left blank, auto-calculated from perimeter of all openings

step25.intWallTooltip: Use the same number from Step 18 (Interior Plastering) + Step 19 (Ceiling)
step25.ceilTooltip: If ceiling is vinyl/tile, painting may not be needed.
step25.intGradeTooltip: Premium for Anti-mold/UV | Washable for easy cleaning (ideal for kids' room/kitchen)
step25.extGradeTooltip: Premium exterior resists UV fading 5+ years | Elastomeric bridges cracks+leaks
step25.sheenTooltip: Matte = Hides imperfections | Gloss = Easy to clean but shows flaws
step25.accentTooltip: Dark walls (blue/dark green/black) need 30% thicker coat — only specify dark areas
step25.woodworkTooltip: Frames, moldings, cornices — Wood stain covers ~12 m²/gal
step25.colorTooltip: ≥ 3 colors → More leftover paint in cans, adds 5% waste margin

step26.lightingCountTooltip: Count from electrical plan: downlights, recessed, ceiling lights
step26.acCircuitTooltip: Each A/C requires a dedicated circuit
step26.mainBreakerTooltip: Typical 2-story house uses 50A, heavy A/C load uses 63A

step27.bathroomCountTooltip: Count from plan — pipes are calculated automatically
step27.hotWaterTooltip: Heat Pump saves 70% energy but has high initial cost
step27.cleanoutTooltip: If set to 0, no cleanouts installed, which may cause long-term maintenance issues

step28.meterDistanceTooltip: Distance from water meter to building connection
step28.greaseTrapTooltip: If empty, defaults to 1 set (Legal requirement)
step28.pumpTankTooltip: Required if main water pressure is low
step28.septicOverrideTooltip: Input manual size if specified in plan

step29.curtainRailTooltip: Measure window span + 15cm on each side
step29.doorStopperTooltip: Install on all doors to prevent wall damage

step30.typeTooltip: Instant = Cheaper | Storage = More Hot Water (higher energy use)

step32.alert: Coat 2 uses same areas & grade as Coat 1 (Step 25) — waste drops to 8%
step32.touchUpTooltip: Usually 3-5% of total area for scratches/tool marks

step33.cleaningTooltip: Total usable area — Big Cleaning for dust/paint/cement
step33.pressureTestTooltip: Number of plumbing systems requiring pressure/leak tests
step33.defectTooltip: Lump sum budget to cover minor touch-ups and reworks before handover

step34.buildingAreaTooltip: Total house area (Indoor + Outdoor) used to estimate cleaning crew cost.
